title: How Does a Touchscreen Know Where You Touched?
sources: Mouser, 'Resistive and Capacitive Touch Technology: How Does It Work?': projected capacitive screens use a grid of transparent electrodes (usually indium tin oxide) in rows and columns under the glass

MicroTouch, 'How Projected Capacitive Touch Technology Works': the controller drives the electrodes to create an electric field; a conductive finger draws away charge and changes the capacitance at that intersection, and the controller scans rows/columns to compute the touch location
ScienceABC, 'How does a touch screen respond to touch?': the human body conducts electricity, which is what a capacitive screen senses

Nelson-Miller, 'Why Can't I Wear Gloves With My Touchscreen?' / MCR Safety 'How touch screen gloves work': ordinary glove fabric is an insulator so the screen cannot sense the finger; touchscreen gloves weave in conductive thread

Engadget (2010-02-12) 'Frozen sausage as iPhone stylus' / The Register (2010-02-12): in a cold South Korean winter, iPhone users used snack sausages as a stylus because the meat conducts like a finger, and sausage sales reportedly rose

lines.text: How does your phone know exactly where you touched it?
lines.caps: HOW DOES YOUR *PHONE | KNOW *EXACTLY | WHERE YOU *TOUCHED IT?

lines.text: Well, under the glass there's a see-through grid of tiny wires,
lines.caps: WELL UNDER THE *GLASS | THERE'S A SEE-THROUGH *GRID | OF TINY *WIRES

lines.text: with a small electric charge sitting on every crossing.
lines.caps: WITH A SMALL *ELECTRIC | *CHARGE | SITTING ON EVERY *CROSSING

lines.text: so when your finger gets close, it pulls a little charge away from that spot.
lines.caps: SO WHEN YOUR *FINGER | GETS *CLOSE | IT *PULLS | A LITTLE *CHARGE | AWAY FROM THAT *SPOT

lines.text: The phone scans every row and column many times a second,
lines.caps: THE PHONE *SCANS | EVERY *ROW | AND *COLUMN | MANY *TIMES | A *SECOND

lines.text: finds the crossing where the charge dropped, and that's your tap.
lines.caps: FINDS THE *CROSSING | WHERE THE CHARGE *DROPPED | AND THAT'S YOUR *TAP

lines.text: Here's the twist: that's why normal gloves don't work,
lines.caps: HERE'S THE *TWIST | THAT'S WHY NORMAL *GLOVES | DON'T *WORK

lines.text: because fabric doesn't conduct, so the screen can't feel you.
lines.caps: BECAUSE *FABRIC | DOESN'T *CONDUCT | SO THE SCREEN *CAN'T | FEEL *YOU

lines.text: But a sausage does, and one freezing winter in Korea,
lines.caps: BUT A *SAUSAGE | *DOES | AND ONE *FREEZING | WINTER IN *KOREA

lines.text: people used sausages as phone pens!
No buttons, no pressure, just your electric fingertip.
